source_text: Humanum est, quod dico propter infirmitatem carnis vestrae; sicut enim exhibuistis membra vestra servire immunditiae et iniquitati ad iniquitatem, ita nunc exhibete membra vestra servire iustitiae in sanctificationem [n400] . O praeceptorem Spiritu Dei plenum, vere vas aureum et tubam non concisis stridoribus, sed absolutis vocibus increpantem! Auctoritatem sermoni suo de exhortationis humanitate conciliat.
pass_a_gloss: It is human, what I say on account of the infirmity of your flesh; for as you exhibited your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity unto iniquity, so now exhibit your members to serve justice unto sanctification. O a teacher full of the Spirit of God, truly a golden vessel and a trumpet crying not with cut-off shrieks but with absolute voices! He conciliates authority for his speech from the humanity of exhortation.
pass_b_english: ‘What I say is human, because of the weakness of your flesh. For just as you presented your members to serve impurity and lawlessness for lawlessness, so now present your members to serve righteousness for sanctification’ (Romans 6:19). What a teacher, filled with God’s Spirit! Truly a golden vessel, and a trumpet sounding not broken shrieks but clear notes! He gains authority for his words through the humanity of his exhortation.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: Scripture's destruction of iniquitas is the Law's purpose; keep moral injustice.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
